title: sync --push sends code-lane work as a merge request
goal: kbgit.py sync --push sends content-only commits to the integration remote's main as today; with any code-lane commit it rebases on the integration main, runs the gate and pushes branch code/<id> (the KB-Work id, else the short hash) with the push options merge_request.create, merge_request.target=main, merge_request.auto_merge and merge_request.remove_source_branch; a remote that does not advertise push options gets the plain branch and the command prints that a merge or pull request must be opened from it; tests.py -k code_lane proves both against local bare remotes (receive.advertisePushOptions on and off)

gates.question: May sync --push push code/<id> branches (not main) to the integration remote and open merge requests there?
options: yes, code/<id> branches with auto-merge; the branch is deleted on merge
yes, but without auto-merge: a person merges
no: code stays on direct push
gates.recommendation: yes, code/<id> branches with auto-merge; the branch is deleted on merge

notes: On a GitLab without merged results pipelines the branch is tested as pushed, so sync rebases right before the push (automated-merge-requests.md:54). Auto-merge is cancelled by new commits on main under fast-forward or semi-linear merge methods (automated-merge-requests.md:24); git.md recommends the merge-commit method as optional host setup.
